title: SRE
description: SRE overview: golden signals per service, 30-day SLO and error budget, incidents with MTTR, deploys and restarts. Objectives: 99.5% of requests not 5xx, 99% within 1s.

list.name: New image deployed
list.expr: (count by (name, image) (container_last_seen{name!="", image!=""}) unless count by (name, image) (container_last_seen{name!="", image!=""} offset 10m)) and on (name) (time() - container_start_time_seconds{name!=""} < 120)

list.name: service
list.label: Service
list.description: Service name from Beyla (beyla/beyla.yml) or the app's own /metrics.

options.content: **Golden signals**: traffic, errors, latency and saturation for each service right now. **SLO**: share of good requests over 30 days and how much of the error budget is left (100% = untouched, 0% = objective missed). **Incidents**: alerts in the selected range, how long they lasted on average (MTTR). **Changes**: deploys and restarts, the usual cause of incidents.

panels.title: Services
panels.description: Traffic (requests/s), errors (share of 5xx), latency (p95 and share over 1s) and saturation (CPU cores of the container with the same name, when there is one).

panels.title: SLO and error budget — last 30 days
SLO by service
panels.description: Availability = share of requests without 5xx (objective 99.5%). Fast = share within 1s (objective 99%). Budget left: 100% untouched, 0% objective missed. Burn 1h: 1 = spending the budget exactly on schedule, 14 = the month's budget gone in about 2 days. Averages of 5-minute ratios, so idle hours weigh as much as busy ones.

panels.title: Error budget left over time
panels.description: Rolling 30-day budget. A steady slope down = errors all the time; a cliff = one incident.

panels.title: Burn rate (1h)
panels.description: How fast the error budget is spent. Above 14.4 for an hour pages (AppErrorBudgetFastBurn).

panels.title: Critical incidents
panels.description: Critical alert episodes that started in the range (a re-fire of the same alert counts again).

panels.title: Time in critical
panels.description: Sum of how long each critical alert was firing.

panels.title: MTTR (critical)
panels.description: Mean time to recover: time in critical / critical incidents. Approximate (15s resolution).

panels.title: Availability (probes)
panels.description: Websites and ports probed by blackbox, whole range.

panels.title: Alerts in range
panels.description: Every alert that fired in the range: how often, total firing time, and average duration of one episode.

targets.expr: sum by (alertname, severity) (count_over_time(ALERTS{alertstate="firing"}[$__range])) * 15 / sum by (alertname, severity) (changes(ALERTS_FOR_STATE[$__range]) + 1)

panels.title: Changes — deploys and restarts in the selected range
Deploys
panels.description: Image changes: a container that ran more than one image in the range (deploy or rollback).

targets.expr: (count(count by (name, image) (count_over_time(container_last_seen{name!="", image!=""}[$__range]))) - count(count by (name) (count_over_time(container_last_seen{name!="", image!=""}[$__range])))) or vector(0)

panels.title: Critical alerts after a deploy
panels.description: Critical alerts firing now while some container changed image in the last hour: a likely bad deploy.

targets.expr: count(count by (alertname) (ALERTS{alertstate="firing", severity="critical"} and on () (count(count by (name, image) (count_over_time(container_last_seen{name!="", image!=""}[1h]))) > count(count by (name) (count_over_time(container_last_seen{name!="", image!=""}[1h])))))) or vector(0)

panels.title: Deploys and restarts by container
panels.description: Only containers with at least one deploy or restart matter; sort by a column to find them.

panels.title: Open ports — listeners on the host and what the internet can reach (port-watch)
Exposed, not allowed
panels.description: Ports reachable on PUBLIC_IP that are not in ALLOWED_PUBLIC_PORTS. Above 0 for 10 minutes = PortExposed.

panels.title: Open on purpose
panels.description: Reachable ports listed in ALLOWED_PUBLIC_PORTS (ssh, http, https...).

panels.title: Listening on all interfaces
panels.description: Candidates for exposure: bound to 0.0.0.0 or ::, not to 127.0.0.1.

panels.title: Exposure check
panels.description: Blind = no port answers on PUBLIC_IP, not even allowed ones (wrong PUBLIC_IP or no hairpin NAT).

panels.title: Listening ports
panels.description: Every TCP listener on the host. Internet: yes = PUBLIC_IP:port accepted a connection. Empty = bound to a local address, not checked.
